candidate.blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential, Related Activity Statements, printed p.13 / PDF p.17: perform focused assessments; recognize trends and changes in client condition and intervene as needed
candidate.blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — focused abdominal assessment
candidate.educational_objective: Perform focused abdominal assessment in the correct sequence by auscultating bowel sounds before palpating the abdomen.

options.B: Apply deep pressure over the most tender area
options.C: Ask the client to contract the abdominal muscles
options.D: Palpate all quadrants rapidly to stimulate peristalsis

candidate.rationale: NCBI Nursing Skills states that abdominal assessment differs from many other physical examinations because bowel sounds should be auscultated before palpation. Palpation can stimulate or otherwise alter bowel activity and make the subsequent bowel-sound assessment less accurate. Therefore A is the correct sequence. Tender areas are assessed last, and the nurse should not intentionally tense the abdominal wall or stimulate peristalsis before auscultation.
candidate.source_claim_supported: During abdominal assessment, bowel sounds should be auscultated before palpation because palpation can alter bowel activity and the sounds being assessed.
candidate.source_locator: Objective Assessment: palpation should occur after auscultation of bowel sounds so accurate, undisturbed bowel sounds can be assessed; Auscultation section: auscultation follows inspection for more accurate assessment of bowel sounds
candidate.source_organization: National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) — Open RN Nursing Skills
candidate.stem: A nurse is performing a focused abdominal assessment on a client with new abdominal distention. Which action should the nurse take before palpating the abdomen?
